question.text: Value at Risk (VaR) of 95% one-month VaR = Rs. 1 crore means:

answer.text: The fund WILL lose Rs. 1 crore over next month
There is 95% probability the loss over next month will NOT exceed Rs. 1 crore
The fund gains Rs. 1 crore with 95% confidence

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 6.2.5.4, 95% one-month VaR = Rs. 1 crore means 95% probability that the fund will NOT lose more than Rs. 1 crore over next month. The Trap: VaR is a probabilistic loss estimate, not a guaranteed loss or gain; not the hurdle. Cross-Exam Context: Standard risk management concept. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Remember VaR's key limitation: it doesn't tell you HOW BAD the 5% tail loss could be — use CVaR/Expected Shortfall for that.
